title: Relaxed adsorption structures
input_files: final extxyz or relaxed xyz files
key_message: Vacancies reconstruct and provide distinct metal coordination
caveat: Use identical camera scale colors and cell display across panels.

title: Li and Na adsorption on pristine and monovacancy graphene
key_message: Both metals bind more strongly at the vacancy and Li binds more strongly than Na
caveat: Literature markers use different cells codes and basis sets.

title: Defect enhancement and metal selectivity
key_message: Vacancy strengthening is 1.55 eV for Li and 1.45 eV for Na
caveat: Plot positive strengthening magnitudes and state the sign convention in the caption.

title: Relaxed height and magnetic response
key_message: Li sits closer than Na and vacancy adsorption modifies the magnetic moment
caveat: Heights and moments come from 6x6x1 relaxations rather than final 9x9x1 SCFs.

title: Numerical convergence of pristine graphene
key_message: Chosen settings are near the predefined approximately 1 meV per carbon threshold
caveat: Use a horizontal 1 meV per carbon guide and preserve signed smearing differences.

title: Adsorption energies and available cutoff validation
series_or_panels: 65/520 Ry for all four systems; 70/560 Ry for pristine systems
key_message: Pristine Li and Na shift by 2.10 and 10.59 meV while the accepted vacancy adsorption energies are retained for context
caveat: The 70/560 Ry vacancy values were not calculated and are explicitly marked unavailable.

title: Residual force check
key_message: Every accepted relaxation lies below the force-component threshold
caveat: Pristine C50 is far below the other values and may need a broken or log axis.

title: Available numerical checks for vacancy-containing systems
series_or_panels: Li/C49 cutoff check; C49 Li/C49 and Na/C49 k-point refinement
key_message: 55/440 differs from 65/520 by 2.736 meV/C for fixed Li/C49 geometry while 6x6x1-to-9x9x1 final-energy shifts are at most 0.026 meV/C
caveat: These are two-point checks; no full vacancy cutoff or smearing sweep and no 70/560 Ry vacancy adsorption-energy calculation exist.
